requirements.requirement: Repair bin/control so start, stop, and status correctly distinguish a live worker, a stale PID, and a PID belonging to another process.
requirements.summary: The repaired controller was installed with valid shell syntax. Direct tests showed stale and foreign PID reporting, stale/foreign PID-file replacement on start, live-worker detection, clean live/stale stops, and foreign-process-safe stop behavior. The same stale-PID recovery succeeded after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Repeated starts must retain a single worker.
requirements.summary: Before and after reboot, repeated starts retained the same PID and process enumeration showed exactly one worker. The final recovered state also contained exactly one live worker.

requirements.requirement: Stopping the worker must leave unrelated processes running.
requirements.summary: A deliberately referenced unrelated sleep process was identified as foreign, survived the controller's stop action, and was only terminated separately during test cleanup. Starting with its PID also left it running.
The original 37-byte B100 record remained as the journal prefix, its inode remained 256038, and normal worker ticks appended through testing and reboot recovery.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The node remained Ubuntu 16.04.7 with kernel 4.4.0-210-generic across execution and reboot. The controller passed POSIX-shell syntax validation and used the existing Python 2.7 worker environment.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied. Direct behavioral tests cover live, stale, and foreign PID handling; singleton starts; unrelated-process safety; journal preservation; and legacy-platform compatibility. The node-restart protocol is complete: a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, restart was acknowledged, the boot ID changed consistently with the fixed lifecycle observations, and service, journal, OS, and kernel state were recovered and reverified.
limitations: Requirement R4 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Installing the controller, starting/stopping workers, creating bounded foreign-process tests, and exercising stale PID files were directly tied to required behavior; each foreign test process was explicitly cleaned up. The reboot served the mandatory restart protocol. The failed non-privileged installation attempt has no evidence of changing state. Final lifecycle observations show no failed services, package damage, unsafe socket exposure, or executor-created temporary-file residue.
